Cement mixers tend to operate more in the afternoon on rural roads and in the morning on urban roads. Agricultural vehicles operate between 4 a.m. and 8 p.m. on weekdays with more miles driven in the morning on urban other roads and a bimodal morning and evening peak on urban freeways. Agricultural vehicles do not tend to start as early on urban other roads on weekends. 86 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Figure 67. Hour VMT fractions by CE-CERT vocation for combination-unit short-haul vehicles In Figure 68, we see that street sweepers drive most miles after 2 p.m. and before 4 a.m., avoiding all morning and midday traffic. Freeway work vehicles follow a similar trend on urban freeways on the weekend. In contrast, utility trucks from the CE-CERT data set operate primarily from 6 a.m. to 3 p.m. on urban roads on weekdays. Beverage delivery trucks drive most miles from 5 a.m. to 9 a.m. Local moving trucks ramp up around 6 a.m. and drive steadily until midnight on urban other roads. On weekdays, towing trucks start around 5 a.m.; on freeways, they have a peak of miles driven at 7 a.m. and finish by 5 p.m., whereas they work rather steadily on urban other roads on weekdays from 5 a.m. to midnight. 87 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications.
